entries.title: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) - Chemical characterisation of brick clay and SSA
entries.description_verbatim:
Material characterisation: brick clay (yellow and red) and sewage sludge ashes (raw, ED-treated and A2P-treated)

The chemical composition was determined by semi-quantitative analysis by XRF with a Malvern PanAnalytical Epsilon 4 EDXRF, on fused beads. Fused beads were prepared by mixing 1.6 g of powder sample with 10 g of fluxing agent: 67% lithium tetraborate and 33% lithium metaborate. Oxide content was reported as a percentage of the total sum of measured oxides, including loss on ignition at 1050°C (LoI1050), determined by heating 1 g of the sample for 15 minutes.
entries.geometry: 1.6 g powder + 10 g flux fused bead
entries.coverage: single DTU study; within-study associations only; source identity is declared rather than independent chain-of-custody
entries.normalization: preserve source oxide+LOI basis; no normalization to oxide-only total or phase fractions

entries.title: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) of brick clay and sewage sludge ash
entries.description_verbatim: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) was conducted on dried brick clay (7 days, 50°C) and dried SSA (24 h, 105°C). Samples (35-40 mg) were crushed in a mortar to ≤ 63 μm and placed in an aluminium oxide crucible in a NETZSCH STA 449 F3 Jupiter. The temperature-dependent mass loss was measured from 35 to 900°C, heating rate 10°C/min, and the cell was purged with 50 ml/min nitrogen gas.
entries.geometry: powder in Al2O3 crucible; recorded mass per curve in conditions.json
entries.coverage: single DTU study; within-study associations only; source identity is declared rather than independent chain-of-custody

entries.title: Brick discs with sewage sludge ash: Production data, water absorption, porosity and density measurements
entries.description_verbatim: Loss of mass from firing (mfired -m105) was calculated for all brick discs. Firing shrinkage was measured for all brick discs as the shrinkage in diameter. Three measurements of the diameter of each disc were made with a digital calliper. Open porosity, water absorption, and dry density were determined on 3 discs for each test series. The discs were placed in a sealed desiccator under a vacuum for 3 h. After 3 h, the discs were submerged in distilled water, under a vacuum for 1 h, whereafter air was led into the chamber and the discs remained in water at atmospheric pressure for 24 h. The saturated discs were weighed first underwater (msw), then dabbed with a cloth and weighed immediately after above water (mssd). The following properties were calculated: Volume, volume of open pores, apparent density, solid density, porosity, water-solids ratio in vacuum water-saturated surface dry conditions.
entries.geometry: small pressed discs; nominal 4 g green; actual mm readings in observations.csv
entries.coverage: single DTU study; within-study associations only; source identity is declared rather than independent chain-of-custody

entries.title: Particle size distribution of sewage sludge ash
entries.description_verbatim: Particle size distribution of SSA was performed on dried and milled samples (24 h, 105°C), and analysed by laser diffraction, using a Malvern Mastersizer 2000, with ethanol as the dispersion medium.
